# SortZone's afterEach leaks a halved drag dwell into every later spec

## Context

PR #18174 (`Resolves #18173`) went red on `unit` in CI at [run 33737551415](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33737551415/job/100591868953) while passing every local arm. @neo-opus-ada independently armed `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` 3085 times locally without a single reproduction and reported it as "a real CI-only unit failure I cannot reproduce".

It is not reproducible from that file because the defect is not in it. `test/playwright/unit/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.spec.mjs` mutates the shared `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` singleton and never restores the engine value.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-03T09:31:02Z; no equivalent found. Closed-queue sweep on `nativeWindowDropDwellMs` returns only #18115 (the feature, closed). Own-assignment sweep: no same-surface hit. Memory Core rationale sweep surfaced the *class* as recurring but not this instance — see Related.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/unit/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.spec.mjs:60` runs an `afterEach` whose stated purpose is to undo the suite's mutations. It is careful and well-commented about the five stubbed methods below it — its own comment says *"a stub that survives its suite is indistinguishable from the method simply not working"*. Two lines above those deletions it does this:

```js
DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs  = 450;
DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropSettleMs = 250;
```

No original is captured anywhere in the file. These are the values *this fixture* wants, written in the place where the *engine's* values belong. The engine defaults are `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:31` `nativeWindowDropDwellMs: 1200` and `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:89` `nativeWindowDropSettleMs: 250`.

`nativeWindowDropSettleMs` happens to coincide with its default, so it is harmless today and harmful the moment the default moves. `nativeWindowDropDwellMs` does not coincide: **after this suite runs, every later spec sharing the worker sees a dwell of 450 instead of 1200.**

Whether `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` lands in that worker after `SortZone.spec.mjs` is worker-assignment order. That is why it is CI-only, and why Playwright reports it as `1 flaky` — it passes on the retry, because **a retry gets a fresh worker, so a cross-file isolation leak heals by construction on every re-run.** The job still exits 1.

### Both CI numbers fall out of the leak exactly

The failing assertion is `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:817`, `expect(delays.at(-1)).toBe(DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs - 600)`.

| Reported | Arithmetic | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `Expected: -150` | `450 - 600` | The assertion re-reads the config at assertion time and gets the **leaked** 450, not 1200. A negative expectation is itself the tell: the test cannot mean to expect a negative remaining hold. |
| `Received: 250` | `Math.max(0, 450 - 600)` → `0` | With dwell at 450 the hold is already spent by frame 3, so `DragCoordinator.mjs:1234` clamps the remainder to `0` and the gesture **completes mid-test**. The commit then schedules the settle timer, so `delays.at(-1)` is the 250ms settle interval, not a dwell remainder. |

At the true default of 1200 the same three frames leave `1200 - 600 = 600` remaining, the hold stays armed, no settle timer is scheduled, and the assertion holds. The test is sound; it is measuring a coordinator whose dwell another file quietly halved.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` is a **singleton**, resolved through the `Neo.manager` namespace and shared by every spec in a Playwright worker. There is no per-spec instance to isolate behind.
- `test/playwright/unit/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.spec.mjs:60-90` — the `afterEach`. Its stub-deletion block is correct (it `delete`s own properties to re-expose the prototype). The two config assignments above it are the defect: assignment where restoration was intended.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:31` / `:89` — the declared defaults, and the only authority for what "restore" means.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:1234` — `dwellRemaining = Math.max(0, me.nativeWindowDropDwellMs - (now - firstSeenAt))`, the clamp that converts the leaked value into a *completed* gesture rather than an obviously wrong number.
- `test/playwright/unit/manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:812` — the victim, not the culprit.

Note `SortZone.spec.mjs:641` and `:725` also set `nativeWindowDropDwellMs: 0`, but those are per-fixture config objects, not singleton writes, and are out of scope here.

## The Fix

In `test/playwright/unit/draggable/dashboard/SortZone.spec.mjs`, capture the engine's own values once before the suite mutates them and restore *those*, so the restore cannot drift from the default:

- Read `nativeWindowDropDwellMs` and `nativeWindowDropSettleMs` off the singleton in a `beforeAll` (or at first `beforeEach`) into module-scoped constants.
- In `afterEach`, assign the captured values back instead of the literals `450` / `250`.

The suite may still set the dwell to 450 *while it runs* — that is a legitimate fixture need. What it may not do is hand 450 to the next spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SortZone.spec.mjs` captures the engine defaults rather than hardcoding `450` / `250` in its `afterEach`.
- [ ] After the full `SortZone.spec.mjs` suite completes, `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs === 1200` and `nativeWindowDropSettleMs === 250`.
- [ ] **Mutation-verified both ways:** with the fix reverted, running `SortZone.spec.mjs` and `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` in that order **in a single worker** fails at `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:817` with `Expected: -150 / Received: 250`; with the fix applied, the same ordered single-worker run passes. A green run alone does not satisfy this AC — the red arm must be demonstrated, and it must be red *for this reason*.
- [ ] Changing `nativeWindowDropDwellMs` in `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs` does not require a corresponding edit in `SortZone.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] PR #18174's `unit` job reaches green with zero `flaky` entries.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` or to the #18173 dwell-restart behaviour it covers. That test is correct as written.
- The `nativeWindowDropDwellMs: 0` fixture configs at `SortZone.spec.mjs:641` / `:725` — per-instance config, not singleton state.
- A general sweep for other singleton-leaking specs. Worth doing, and it is not this ticket; see #17922 for the adjacent coverage lane.
- Any change to how Playwright assigns specs to workers, or to `failOnFlakyTests`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Retrying, quarantining, or `test.retry`-ing `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:812`.** The industry-default response to a `flaky` label is to re-run or mark it flaky. Here the retry *is the mask*: a fresh worker heals the leak by construction, so "it passed on re-run" is the signature of an isolation defect, not evidence of runner variance. Quarantining would have discarded a correct test and left the leak to hit the next arrival.
- **Hunting the defect inside `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs`.** 3085 local arms of that file could not have reproduced it; the file is the victim. The discriminating instrument is a two-file, single-worker ordered run — nothing scoped to one file can see a cross-file leak.
- **"Fixing" the assertion to expect 450.** It would go green and cement the leak as the contract, and the negative expectation (`-150`) would have been left standing as if intended.
- **Adding a defensive re-assert of the default at the top of `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs`.** That treats the symptom at the victim and leaves every *other* later spec in the worker exposed.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this is a test-isolation defect, not an architectural change. The engine defaults at `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:31`/`:89` remain the single source of authority; the fix makes the spec derive from them instead of restating them.

## Two corrections to this ticket, from the instrument rather than from reading

I filed this from CI logs during a heartbeat and reasoned the mechanism out rather than measuring it. Two things in the body above are wrong, and a third is now unreachable. Correcting them here rather than silently shipping a fix that contradicts its own ticket.

### 1. The leaked value is `0`, not `450`

The body says every later spec sees a dwell of 450. It does not. Removing the `afterEach` assignment and asserting the post-suite state directly gives:

```
Error: the suite hands the next spec the dwell it was given
Expected: 1200
Received: 0
```

The `= 450` line was a **partial mask**. It overwrote a `0` that the suite had already left on the singleton, so the value that escaped into CI was the milder of the two. Reading the line as "an assignment where a restore belongs" was right; reading 450 as the leaked value was wrong — 450 is what the mask published, not what the suite produced.

### 2. The `Object.assign` blocks are the source, and they are not out of scope

The **Out of Scope** section says the `nativeWindowDropDwellMs: 0` sites are "per-fixture config objects, not singleton writes". They are singleton writes:

```js
Object.assign(DragCoordinator, {
    nativeWindowDropDwellMs : 0,
    nativeWindowDropSettleMs: 0,
    ...
});
```

`DragCoordinator` there is `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` itself. Two tests do this so the hold commits synchronously — a legitimate fixture need — and they are the actual origin of the leak. I classified them on their shape (an object literal of configs) instead of on what they are assigned *to*.

### 3. AC-3's red arm no longer exists at the named victim

AC-3 asks for a red at `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:817` with `Expected: -150 / Received: 250`. The second commit on the merged PR #18174 pinned that arm:

```js
originalDwell = DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs,
DWELL_MS      = 1200;   // PINNED, never read from the live config
```

That was the right call for #18174 and it makes the victim immune — so the reproducer named in AC-3 cannot be produced any more. Worth noting the `finally` restores `originalDwell`, i.e. whatever ambient value it found: the pin protects that file and **preserves** the leak for whoever follows.

### Revised AC-3

> **Mutation-verified both ways:** with the restore reverted to the literals `450` / `250`, the `afterAll` witness in `SortZone.spec.mjs` fails with `Expected: 1200 / Received: 450`; with the restore deleted outright it fails with `Received: 0`; with the fix applied the suite passes. A green run alone does not satisfy this AC — the red arm must be demonstrated, and it must be red *for this reason*.

Evidence for all three arms is in the PR.

### What did not change

AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 and AC-5 stand as written, and the diagnosis that this is a cross-file singleton leak masquerading as a flake — with a retry healing it by construction — holds exactly. The fix is still confined to `SortZone.spec.mjs`.
